newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish vehicle exports fall 32 pct in Jan-May.
newsitem.headline: Turkish vehicle exports fall 32 pct in Jan-May.

text.p: The value of Turkish vehicle exports fell 32 percent to $165.4 million in January-May 1997 compared to $244.1 million in the same period last year, the Automotive Industry Association (OSD) said on Wednesday.

Car exports dived 63 percent to $52.7 million in the first five months of the year, accounting for the bulk of the overall fall, the OSD said. Exports of buses meanwhile, rose by nine percent to $89.7 million.
Overall Turkish automotive exports fell nine percent to $524.2 million in January-May this year.

Exports for allied automotive industries rose by eight percent in total to $358.8 million, from $331.9 million in the first five months of 1996. They were led by tyre exports which firmed three percent to $99.8 million.
The OSD said domestic car sales in the first five months of this year rose 37 percent to 110,699, from 80,962 a year ago, due to a 131 percent jump to 35,718 in sales of imported cars.

Sales of domestic cars firmed by only 14.5 percent to 74,981 units, so the share of imported cars in the domestic market leapt to a five-year high 32 percent in January-May 1997, compared to 19 percent in the same 1996 period.

Turkey's total automotive output was up seven percent to 144,250 in January-May this year, including 88,550 cars, down two percent from the first five months of 1996. The rise in commercial vehicle production was 53 percent to 35,036 units.
